newsitem.title: UK: UK Treasury to re-publish Building Societies Bill.
newsitem.headline: UK Treasury to re-publish Building Societies Bill.

text.p: The UK Treasury said it intends to re-publish the Building Societies Bill with amendments taking into account representations made to it over the Summer, a Treasury spokesman told Reuters on Wednesday.
The measure was unexpectedly omitted from the Queen's Speech outlining the government's legislative programme in the forthcoming parliamentary session.
The spokesman said the bill might still be introduced in the session depending on the time available and how much support it received.
Earlier, the Building Societies Association (BSA) said it was disappointed that the Bill was not included in the Speech.
It said it hoped the bill would still be introduced.

"We are perplexed that, given the government's declared support for building societies and the months of hard work that have been put into drafting it, the new Bill has been deferred," said BSA chairman Brian Davis.
He urged the government to find parliamentary time for the bill, which it said is "relatively non-controversial."
Davis said the proposed legislation would be less prescriptive and give the societies the greatest possible flexibility to respond to changing customer needs.

But Davis called on the Treasury to exclude what it called the "anti-competitive position under which a converted (to bank status) society is protected from takeover for five years, but can itself seek to acquire other building societies, which do not share the benefit of takeover protection."

The new Bill is basically a deregulatory measure which will give the societies more freedom as long as 75 percent of their lending is on housing and they raise a minimum of 50 percent of their funds from their members. -- Joe Ortiz, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717.
